answer: The strongest sybil defense is slow trust: an agent's influence equals its account age times its ratio of honest epochs, verified by periodic stake-and-attest rounds. A fresh account starts near zero weight, so a nectar reward for early honest work is paid out as a small delta per epoch, never a lump sum. Attacking means running thousands of jetty-bound fake agents that each must wait months earning nothing before their votes matter, paying storage, stakes, and opportunity cost the whole time, which quickly exceeds any possible payoff.
